boundary: VERIFIED: the rank-32 qubit tower has four rungs, 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 qubits, bottoming at W(3,2) via an order-16 element that W(E8) does not contain. THE UNIFIED KERNEL LAW -- dim K = k(p-1)/p, dim K-perp = k/p, rank(F|K) = k(p-2)/p, so the kernel is ALWAYS coisotropic and Lagrangian exactly at p=2 -- was predicted from p=2,3 and confirmed at p=5 on rank 40 with all three numbers exact. THE LIFT THEOREM: tau_p . diag(a,I,..,I) preserves the multiplicity j, hence the geometry, so L^p carries L's geometry at rank pr. Therefore the E8^3-versus-Leech asymmetry is about DECOMPOSABILITY, not rank 24

lift_theorem.consequence: the geometry W(j-1,p) is determined by j and p, so the lifted geometry EQUALS the base geometry: a geometry-preserving rank multiplier
lift_theorem.one_factor_generates: the class map restricted to a single E8 factor already has full rank on the lifted quotient
lift_theorem.statement: if a has char poly Phi_{p^m}^j on rank r then g = tau_p . diag(a,I,..,I) on L^p (rank pr) has char poly Phi_{p^{m+1}}^j -- the SAME j -- since deg Phi_{p^{m+1}} = p deg Phi_{p^m}

not_done: whether an indecomposable lattice admits a lift by another mechanism

rank32_tower.bottom: W(3,2), the doily, two qubits -- requiring order 16, which W(E8) does not contain; the 4-cycle supplies it
rank32_tower.element: tau_4 . diag(M,I,I,I) with M the E8 order-4 Phi_4^4 element

the_asymmetry_reread.consequence: the presence of W(3,3) at rank 24 is a fact about DECOMPOSABILITY, not about rank; 'Co0 has no Phi_9^4 class' is what indecomposability looks like from the character table
the_asymmetry_reread.old_statement: E8^3 reaches W(3,3) at rank 24 and Leech does not
the_asymmetry_reread.prediction: for any L with a geometry at rank r, L^p carries the same geometry at rank pr, at element order p times higher
the_asymmetry_reread.sharper: E8^3 does not discover a W(3,3); it INHERITS E8's own, carried by the 3-cycle. Leech is INDECOMPOSABLE, has no factors to permute, and so has nothing to inherit

unified_kernel_law.lagrangian_iff: dim K = k/2 requires (p-1)/p = 1/2, i.e. p = 2 alone
unified_kernel_law.reading: Lagrangian is not a separate phenomenon; it is the p=2 case of coisotropic, where K-perp equals K instead of merely sitting in it
unified_kernel_law.statement: descending one rung at prime p divides the quotient dimension by p, so dim K = k(p-1)/p, dim K-perp = k/p, and if K is coisotropic rank(F|K) = k(p-2)/p
